findings.checklist_item: Specify that the archive-time inline fold invokes the single-ticket fold with horizon=0 and threshold=0 (fold-everything) so it converges regardless of event age/count, not the ordinary horizon/threshold-gated fold.
evidence: compact_txn.py:478 `if event_count <= threshold: ... skipping compaction`
compact_txn.py:491-496 `old = [... if is_foldable(ts, now, horizon)]; if not old: 'all events within the compaction horizon — nothing to fold'; return 0`
Plan: 'rebar archive performs the ticket's final fold inline (reusing the existing single-ticket fold path compact_txn already exposes)' — parameters unspecified
AC1: 'rebar archive folds the ticket inline (SNAPSHOT covers all its events)'
findings.finding: The archive-time inline fold does not specify the horizon/threshold it invokes _compact_locked with; the shared single-ticket fold path folds ONLY events older than the compaction horizon and ONLY when the event count exceeds the threshold, so a just-archived hot ticket (all tail events within-horizon) or a small ticket (below threshold) would fold nothing and write no SNAPSHOT.
scenarios: Archiving a ticket whose tail events are all newer than compact.COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS
Archiving a ticket with fewer live events than compact.threshold
findings.suggested_fix: State that archive calls the fold path with horizon=0, threshold=0 (matching the compact-all sweep's `--threshold=0`) so every live event is folded at archive time regardless of the configured horizon/threshold.

No stated behavior for a crash between fold and ARCHIVED write, or a fold that fails
findings.finding: The inline archive fold happens 'right before writing the ARCHIVED event' but the plan does not state the failure/partial-state behavior if the process dies between the fold and the ARCHIVED write, or if the inline fold itself errors.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (leaf.py) — 'performs the ticket's final fold inline ... right before writing the ARCHIVED event'
scenarios: Process interrupted after fold succeeds but before ARCHIVED event is written
Inline fold raises on a corrupt event file during archive
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach step 1 noting the fold is idempotent and that ARCHIVED (net-archived confirmation) is what makes the ticket skippable, so an interrupted archive leaves the ticket active and self-heals on retry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the archive-time fold in the shared archive write seam (the archive `*_core`/append-ARCHIVED path) rather than only in leaf.py, so MCP and library archive callers inherit the 'archived => folded' invariant and cannot strand unfolded events under the new active-only default.
evidence: 'leaf.archive (src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py) writes only the ARCHIVED event + .archived marker'
'make the fold part of the archive operation itself: rebar archive performs the ticket's final fold inline ... right before writing the ARCHIVED event'
Bypassing ingress paths: MCP server archive tool handler; library archive facade — if they append the ARCHIVED event through the shared write path rather than through leaf.py.
findings.finding: The archive-time inline fold is placed in the CLI command `leaf.archive` (src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py). If `rebar archive` is also reachable via a library facade or MCP tool that does not route through this CLI command's fold call, those ingress paths write the ARCHIVED event without the inline fold, so the new invariant 'an archived ticket is folded on its way out' holds only for the CLI. Because the default scoping (change 2) makes the sweep skip archived tickets entirely, an MCP/library archive that bypasses the fold would strand unfolded tail events with no default path ever folding them.
findings.location: Approach step 1 / Scope: 'src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py — archive performs the ticket's terminal fold inline before the ARCHIVED event.'
scenarios: A library caller invoking the archive facade directly appends ARCHIVED without the leaf.py inline fold; the ticket is archived-but-unfolded and the default active-only sweep never revisits it — stranded events until an --include-archived run.
An MCP `archive` tool call routes through the server handler, not the CLI command, skipping the inline fold with the same stranding consequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the inline fold to the shared core function that writes the ARCHIVED event (the seam all three ingress paths call) so the fold precedes the ARCHIVED append for every surface, and verify the sequence test drives at least one non-CLI path.

findings.checklist_item: Clarify the atomicity and event coverage of the inline fold: whether fold+ARCHIVED-append are one locked unit or two, and restate AC1 to acknowledge the trailing ARCHIVED event stays a live tail event outside the just-written SNAPSHOT.
evidence: Plan: 'performs the ticket's final fold inline ... right before writing the ARCHIVED event'
leaf.py:173 `append_event(resolved, 'ARCHIVED', {}, ...)` — separate locked write
compact_txn.py:461 `lock.acquire(tracker, ...)` — the fold takes the store write lock itself
findings.finding: The plan does not address the ordering/atomicity of the inline fold relative to the ARCHIVED append: the fold runs 'right before writing the ARCHIVED event', so the ARCHIVED event is never captured by the snapshot, and the fold (which takes the store write lock) and the subsequent ARCHIVED append are two separate locked operations with no stated atomicity.
scenarios: A crash between the inline fold and the ARCHIVED append
AC1's literal reading 'SNAPSHOT covers ALL its events' vs the ARCHIVED event necessarily living outside the snapshot
